To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. The majority (two-thirds) of Canadian employers have implemented one or more of the nine innovations studied; 2. The most frequently adopted innovations were employee participation in decision making, job enrichment, and quality circles, while the least frequently adopted innovations were gain sharing and work teams; 3. The most common time period for the implementation of innovations was 1980 to 1985;

(1) a majority of Canadian firms have adopted some form of workplace innovation in the past 25 years; (2) the adoption of these innovations is uneven across sectors and industries, and has increased over time, especially since 1980; (3) the adoption of workplace innovations is associated with a number of other innovations; and (4) the adoption of some innovations is more likely than others to lead to the adoption of others.
